info.title: No Wave REST API
info.description:
This document is generated from the API's own route table (`apps/api/src/transport/rest/routes.ts`), so an endpoint that is not listed here does not exist, and an endpoint that exists is listed here.

Conventions that hold for every operation:

- Bearer authentication: `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Private routes derive the acting account from the token and never accept a client-supplied actor or owner id.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` on JSON responses; uploaded images are immutable and cached for a year.
- JSON write bodies require `Content-Type: application/json`, are limited in size, and reject unsupported fields rather than ignoring them.
- Errors are `{"error":{"code","message"}}` with stable codes; messages are sanitized.
- Article locales are `zh-CN`, `zh-TW` and `en`. An omitted locale means `zh-CN`.
- Discovery lists accept `limit` and `offset`; article discovery also accepts a `cursor` with `sort=latest`.

get.summary: Read the comment tree of a published work

200.description: A page of top-level comments, each with its replies.

400.description: Bad request: `BAD_USER_INPUT` for a query or body the contract does not allow, `BAD_INPUT` for discovery paging misuse.

get.description: `limit` counts **top-level** comments, not replies: each top-level comment arrives with its whole reply tree, so a page boundary never cuts a conversation in half. The order is oldest first, by `(createdAt, id)`. To read further down a long thread, send `cursor` built from the **last top-level comment** of the page already received: `base64url("<createdAt>|<id>")`, using the `createdAt` exactly as returned. Each page is a plain array with no `nextCursor`; keep requesting while a page is non-empty and stop at the first empty one. A reply posted mid-read is newer than the cursor, so it never shifts the roots the reader has not reached yet: it appears under its own root, or not at all on this pass.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Language edition to read. Defaults to `zh-CN` when absent.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `base64url("<createdAt>|<id>")` of the last top-level comment already received. An empty page is the end of the thread.

post.description: A beacon the page sends after it has actually rendered the work — never part of the cached `GET`. Counting is `(work, reader, UTC day)`: one account or one address contributes at most one view per work per day, the author's own reads never count, and a repeat answers `200 {counted: false}` rather than an error. Public: an anonymous reader is counted, keyed by a digest of their address, and no address or account id is stored. A slug that is not a published work answers `404`.

post.description: One path, seven actions, chosen by the `action` path parameter. Bodies are action-specific: `register` and `login` take `{email, password}`; `refresh` and `logout` take `{refreshToken}`; `forgot-password` takes `{email}`; `reset-password` takes `{token, password}`; `verify-email` takes `{token}`. `register` answers `201`, a recovery request answers `202` whether or not the address has an account (an account-enumeration oracle is not an error message), and `forgot-password` / `verify-email` answer `409 MAIL_DISABLED` while mail is switched off.

patch.description: Only the author may edit; somebody else's comment answers `403 FORBIDDEN` and a comment that does not exist answers `404 NOT_FOUND`, the same pair the delete answers. The edit replaces the text, stamps `editedAt` and leaves `createdAt`, the parent link and the idempotency record alone, so the thread keeps its order. No notification is emitted: re-notifying on every edit would let an author page the whole thread at will. Previous text is not retained — there is no revision history in v1 (ADR 0031).

post.summary: Import a Notion database bundle into your own works

200.description: The per-page report (and, with `apply: true`, what was written).

400.description: Bad request: `BAD_USER_INPUT` for a query or body the contract does not allow, `BAD_INPUT` for discovery paging misuse.

401.description: No valid, unrevoked bearer token was presented (`UNAUTHENTICATED`).

413.description: The request body is larger than this route accepts (`PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`).

post.description:
The bundle is a Notion export of one database: its pages, their properties and their blocks. Each work becomes an article owned by the caller; a work's other language versions become article translations of the same article.

**A dry run is the default.** Without `apply: true` nothing is written — no works, no tags, no provenance rows — and `pages` describes exactly what a real run would do. Send `apply: true` to perform those writes.

**Re-importing is idempotent.** The server records which page each edition came from, together with a digest of the content it produced, so importing the same bundle twice reports `skip` and writes nothing; changed pages update the work they already belong to and keep the address it already has. A page that disappeared from Notion is reported, never deleted here, and a work the author deleted is refused rather than recreated.

Pages that cannot become a work (`empty-body`, `empty-title`, and the other `issues` codes) are reported per page instead of failing the request: an import of forty pages does not fail because one of them is empty. Every write carries `Idempotency-Key: notion-seed:<pageId>`, so a request that dies mid-way can be retried without duplicating what it already created.

get.description: Newest first, ordered by `(createdAt, id)`. To read older notices, send `cursor` built from the **last** notification of the page already received: `base64url("<createdAt>|<id>")`, using the `createdAt` exactly as returned. Each page is a plain array with no `nextCursor`; keep requesting while a page is non-empty and stop at the first empty one. A notification that arrives while the reader is paging is newer than the cursor and therefore does not shift the older pages; marking notices read does not change their position. The recipient comes from the token — there is no parameter that selects someone else's inbox.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `base64url("<createdAt>|<id>")` of the last notification already received. An empty page is the end of the inbox.

bearerAuth.description: A signed access token from `POST /auth/login` or `/auth/register`. It names the session it belongs to, so revoking that session stops it working before it expires.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code, for example `BAD_USER_INPUT` or `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.

message.description: Sanitized human-readable message. Internal details are never included.

details.description: Optional structured detail, for example the works that reference a media asset.

id.description: The authenticated account's stable user id.

AuthSession.description: Bearer credentials. Send `accessToken` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; spend `refreshToken` exactly once at `POST /auth/refresh`.

current.description: True for the session that made this request.

revokedSessions.description: How many other sessions were signed out. The asking session is spared.

alreadyVerified.description: An address that was already verified is not mailed again.

AuthorProfile.description: A member's public profile, plus the viewer-specific follow state when a token was presented.

isFollowing.description: True when the authenticated viewer follows this author.

AuthorDirectoryEntry.description: One row of the public author directory: reach and published-work count, no contact details.

Article.description: A stored work plus the `author`, `categories` and `tags` the API adds. One id identifies the work; `(id, locale)` identifies one of its translations.

workType.description: `serial` is retired: it can be read and saved but not chosen for new work.

contentBlocks.description: Application-owned content blocks. Version 0 is text-only (`{id, type, text}`); version 1 adds inline marks and links. Raw Lexical JSON is never stored or returned.

viewCount.description: Readers who opened the work, counted once per reader per UTC day and never the author's own visits (ADR 0035). Work-wide, not per translation.

DeletedArticle.description: A tombstone in the author's recycle bin: the work plus when it was deleted and what its removal will sweep.

ArticleView.description: The answer to a view beacon.

counted.description: Whether this call moved the number. `false` is a normal answer: the author's own read, or a second visit to the same work on the same UTC day.

content.description: Plain-text rendering that matches the versioned blocks.

contentBlocks.description: Application-owned content blocks. Version 0 is text-only (`{id, type, text}`); version 1 adds inline marks and links. Raw Lexical JSON is never stored or returned.

editedAt.description: When the author last corrected the text, or `null` for a comment as written. Previous text is not retained (ADR 0031).

deleted.description: False when the caller does not own the row; ownership failures are not distinguished from absence.

MediaAsset.description: One uploaded, immutable image. The address a content body keeps is `src: /api/media/<id>`.

Notification.description: One inbox row. `userId` is the recipient and is never part of the response.

payload.description: The event payload, serialized as JSON text.

duplicate.description: True when an idempotent replay returned the stored message instead of sending another.

token.description: Base64url single-use token from the recovery mail. Redeemed in the body, never in a path.
Single-use token from the verification mail.

ArticleWrite.description: Create: `title` plus exactly one of `contentBlocks` / `editorState`. Update: `slug` and `publish` are mandatory, and an explicit `locale` replaces that translation of the work. Unknown fields are rejected.

slug.description: Optional on create (derived from the title); mandatory on update.

summary.description: Blank or absent means the server derives one from the body text.

locale.description: Absent keeps the historical `zh-CN` default; a client editing another edition must send its locale.

contentBlocks.description: Version 0 blocks, or version 1 when `contentBlocksVersion` is 1.

editorState.description: Write-only serialized Lexical state. Normalized to `contentBlocks` before storage; requires `contentBlocksVersion: 1`.

workType.description: Types a new work may be created with. `serial` answers 400 on create; a stored `serial` work stays saveable and may be moved to an active type.

CommentWrite.description: Exactly one of `content` (version 0 plain text) or `contentBlocks` / `editorState` (version 1 rich text).

CommentUpdate.description: Exactly one of `content` (version 0 plain text) or `contentBlocks` / `editorState` (version 1 rich text). An edit replaces the text and stamps `editedAt`; it does not re-notify the thread.

ProfileWrite.description: Unsupported fields are rejected. `locale` may only be `zh-CN` today.

FeaturedWrite.description: The whole ordered shelf, not individual moves: two editors cannot interleave into a shelf neither asked for.

TaxonomyCreate.description: A category is editorial (editors only); a tag is the author's own words.

LikeWrite.description: Explicit state, not a toggle, so a retried request cannot flip it back.

NotionBundle.description: A Notion database export: the database, and its pages with their flattened blocks.

properties.description: Notion property values, keyed by property name.

blocks.description: The page body, depth-first and flattened.

NotionImportRequest.description: A dry run unless `apply` is `true`. A dry run is a pure read: it creates no works, no tags, and no links, and its `pages` describe what would happen.

apply.description: `true` performs the writes the report describes.

NotionImportReport.description: One line per page. `applied: false` means nothing was written and every action below is a plan.

externalId.description: The Notion page id this edition came from.

locale.description: The edition's locale; empty for a page that could not become a work.

slug.description: The address of the work this edition belongs to.

detail.description: One line a human can read.

externalDocs.description: Generated-contract guide: how to regenerate, and what the document does and does not claim.
